Mission Local’s four data takeaways were:

- Turnout was 78.9%: above the city’s 77% historical average for presidential elections, but well below 2020’s 86.3%. Roughly 412,000 people voted, about 38,000 fewer than in 2020, despite a similar number of registered voters. A shift of some local races to even-year elections meant more voters than ever participated in races such as mayor and district attorney.
- Results showed geographic divides. Proposition K passed citywide 55–45, despite strong opposition in districts near the Great Highway. Supervisor races also split along neighborhood lines in Districts 7 and 9.
- Money did not guarantee wins. Daniel Lurie’s roughly $16 million mayoral campaign succeeded, but Proposition D raised $9.5 million and lost by 13 points, while competing Proposition E passed after raising about $69,000. Outside spending also supported winners in the close District 1 and District 11 supervisor races.
- Redistricting reshaped some supervisor contests. In District 1’s newly added Seacliff precincts, Marjan Philhour won 52% of first-choice votes, but not enough to defeat Connie Chan. In District 3, Danny Sauter won 45% of first-choice votes in newly added Russian Hill precincts.
